card.name: Mid-sentence words in overdose and safety text
card.fires_on: Single words partway through safety statements in drug labels, such as verbs after animal dose amounts, 'intracellular' in shunting, 'Metabolic' in acidosis headings, and the start of warning lines.

modes.label: Verb after animal dose
modes.description: A verb such as 'are' or 'were' right after a large mg/kg dose in animal lethality sentences.
modes.example: rats and mice given single oral doses of levodopa of approximately 1,500 mg/kg to 2,000 mg/kg<< are>> expected to die.

modes.label: Inside medical terms
modes.description: A word or word part inside a long medical term or heading, such as 'acellular' or 'abolic'.

modes.label: Warning and negation words
modes.description: Short words in warnings or negated safety statements, such as 'IF', 'significantly' or 'harm'.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE Propranolol is not<< significantly>> dialyzable.

card.plain: It lights up on a word in the middle of overdose, animal toxicity or warning sentences in drug labels.
